title: Epoch AI ‘OEIS Open’: Generic Tool-Using LLMs Autonomously Prove or Disprove 147 Open Conjectures in Lean 4
aiSystem: Epoch AI LeanOpenProblems Agent (GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 & Gemini + Lean 4)
whyItMatters: Simple off-the-shelf tool-using LLM agents autonomously proved or disproved 147 of 492 formally stated open OEIS mathematical conjectures in Lean 4—all machine-verified with anti-cheating checks at just $50 per problem.
summary: Posted in August 2026 (arXiv:2608.11941) by Tom Adamczewski at Epoch AI, OEIS Open evaluated generic ReAct-style language models equipped with minimal tools (bash, text editor, and Lean 4) against 492 formally stated open conjectures drawn from the Online Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (auto-formalized by Tsoukalas et al. in Google DeepMind’s Formal Conjectures repository, where DeepMind’s bespoke May 2026 agent had solved 44). Using strict SafeVerify anti-exploit checking to guard against axiom injection, off-the-shelf frontier models autonomously proved or disproved 147 of the 492 open conjectures (30%) at a modest $50 budget per attempt—with subsequent leaderboard updates pushing GPT-6 Astra to 57/100 and Claude Fable 5.1 to 53/100 on OEIS Open Lite—demonstrating scalable, low-cost autonomous mathematical theorem discovery.
technicalHighlights: Resolved 147 of 492 formalized open OEIS conjectures (more than 3× DeepMind’s initial 44/492 baseline) using minimal bash + editor + Lean 4 agent loops at $50/attempt.
Every accepted proof or disproof passed SafeVerify formal kernel checks against the exact theorem specification to prevent axiom-injection cheating.
Released open-source benchmark and evaluation scaffold (epoch-research/LeanOpenProblems), demonstrating that simple generic agent loops match or beat complex bespoke provers.
caveats: As the author explicitly notes, most OEIS conjectures received little prior human mathematician attention and carry lower individual fame than Millennium/Erdős problems; auto-formalized statements also carry residual risk of subtle misformalization.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrated high-volume, reproducible autonomous resolution of open mathematical conjectures by generic tool-using LLMs rather than specialized math engines.
scoreRationale.ripple: Created the open standard benchmark (LeanOpenProblems) directly leading to GPT-6 Astra’s Köthe, Smale, and Dittert formalizations.
scoreRationale.verification: All 147 proofs/disproofs passed Lean 4 + SafeVerify specification checks, though auto-formalized source statements carry slight misformalization caveats.
scoreRationale.velocity: Resolved 147 open conjectures autonomously at $50/attempt—demonstrating mass-scale formal theorem production.
